youtube.title: Columbus Didn't Prove the Earth Was Round. Everyone Already Knew
youtube.description:
Educated Europeans had known the Earth was round since antiquity; around 240 BC Eratosthenes estimated its circumference with shadows and geometry. The real dispute over Columbus's voyage was his math: he greatly underestimated the Earth's size and overestimated Asia's, and his critics were right that the ocean was too wide to cross. The Americas saved him. The flat-Earth version owes much to Washington Irving's 1828 biography of Columbus.

📂 Case File #062: Columbus & the Flat Earth

Sources: History.com, "Christopher Columbus Never Set Out to Prove the Earth was Round" https://www.history.com/news/christopher-columbus-never-set-out-to-prove-the-earth-was-round ; CBS News, "Five misconceptions about Columbus" https://www.cbsnews.com/news/five-misconceptions-about-columbus ; Darin Hayton, "Washington Irving's Columbus and the Flat Earth" https://dhayton.haverford.edu/blog/2014/12/02/washington-irvings-columbus-and-the-flat-earth/
Images: Sebastiano del Piombo (1519); Behaim's Erdapfel (CC BY-SA 2.0 de); Eratosthenes diagram (CC BY-SA 3.0); Washington Irving (PD), via Wikimedia Commons.
